purpose: Start a point by hitting the ball from above the head, at full reach, into the diagonal service box with controlled pace, spin and placement, using a coordinated kinetic chain (legs, hips, trunk, shoulder, arm) and a repeatable toss.

phases.description: Sideways-on stance, weight balanced, racket and ball held low in front; ends as the hands separate and the weight starts to move.

Tossing arm lifts and extends upward while the knees bend and the hitting arm rises to the trophy position (hitting elbow around shoulder height, racket up); ends at deepest knee bend/trophy position.
Racket drops behind the back (elbow bent) while the legs begin to push up; ends at lowest racket position just before the upward drive.
Legs drive up, trunk rotates and the arm extends up and forward to ball contact; ends at contact.
Arm decelerates across the body, the player lands and recovers balance; ends when the motion is complete.

faults.description: Knees stay nearly straight at the trophy position, so little energy is stored from the legs.
faults.cue_intent: Prompt the player to bend the knees and sit into the legs as the arms rise.
faults.ask_if_unsure_intent: Ask whether they feel their legs working in the serve or if it feels all arm.
faults.fix_intent: Teach a deliberate knee bend in the loading phase, e.g. serve in slow motion pausing at trophy with the knees bent.

faults.description: Hitting upper arm is well below shoulder height at the trophy position (dropped elbow), weakening the arm path and shoulder position.
faults.cue_intent: Cue lifting the hitting elbow up to about shoulder height at trophy.
faults.ask_if_unsure_intent: Ask whether the racket arm feels heavy or lazy going up.
faults.fix_intent: Drill the trophy position in front of a mirror, raising the elbow with the tossing arm.

faults.description: Tossing arm does not extend up and is pulled down early, which tends to make the toss inconsistent and the body collapse.
faults.cue_intent: Cue keeping the tossing arm reaching up toward the ball.
faults.ask_if_unsure_intent: Ask where the ball tends to land relative to them and whether the toss varies.
faults.fix_intent: Practice tossing and holding the arm up until contact, aiming the toss to a repeatable spot.

faults.description: Arm remains fairly straight with little elbow bend during the racket drop, reducing the loop and racket lag.
faults.cue_intent: Cue letting the racket fall behind the back with a relaxed, bent elbow.
faults.ask_if_unsure_intent: Ask whether the swing feels like a push or a throw.
faults.fix_intent: Use a relaxed throwing-style motion drill to get a loose racket drop.

faults.description: Hips do not rise up toward the ball by contact, so the body fails to extend and the contact is low and mostly arm-driven.
faults.cue_intent: Cue pushing up through the legs and reaching tall at contact.
faults.ask_if_unsure_intent: Ask whether they feel themselves leaving the ground or extending up into the ball.
faults.fix_intent: Drill an explosive push from a bent-knee trophy into full body extension.

faults.description: Hitting elbow is still clearly bent at contact instead of reaching up with an extended arm.
faults.cue_intent: Cue reaching up to meet the ball with a long arm.
faults.ask_if_unsure_intent: Ask whether the ball is dropping before they hit it or they feel cramped at contact.
faults.fix_intent: Raise the toss and practise reaching up to contact at full extension.

faults.description: Hitting wrist is not high above the shoulder at contact, so the ball is hit low, making it harder to clear the net and reach the box.
faults.cue_intent: Cue hitting the ball at the highest point you can reach.
faults.ask_if_unsure_intent: Ask where the ball is relative to them when they hit it (dropping or at the peak).
faults.fix_intent: Adjust the toss height and finish extension to meet the ball at the top of reach.

faults.description: Shoulders and hips turn together at the trophy position, with little trunk coil to store rotational power.
faults.cue_intent: Cue turning the shoulders further than the hips as the arms rise.
faults.ask_if_unsure_intent: Ask whether the body feels turned sideways during the toss.
faults.fix_intent: Use shadow serves with an exaggerated shoulder turn before the swing.

faults.description: Body does not move forward into the court by contact, so the weight stays back and the swing is more up than through the ball.
faults.cue_intent: Cue transferring the weight up and forward into the shot.
faults.ask_if_unsure_intent: Ask whether they fall backward or sideways after the serve.
faults.fix_intent: Drill a forward weight transfer and landing inside the baseline.

outcomes.description: Ball clears the net and lands in the correct service box.
Ball leaves the racket at high speed through efficient use of the kinetic chain.
The toss lands or peaks at a repeatable spot in front of the hitting shoulder.
Ball is struck at full upward reach with an extended arm.
The serve motion follows the conventional sequence of trophy, racket drop, extension and follow-through.

links.mechanism: A moderate knee bend stores leg drive for the upward push, while too little gives no leg contribution and too much costs timing.
A hitting elbow near shoulder height sets a strong, repeatable arm path into the drop and extension.
Greater shoulder-hip separation lets the trunk rotation stretch and then release, adding racket speed.
Leg extension lifts the whole body so the contact point is higher.
A higher hitting hand gives a steeper angle down over the net into the box.
A near-straight arm at contact maximizes the reach and keeps contact geometry consistent.
A tossing arm extended up and held steady releases the ball vertically at a repeatable point.
Moving the body forward into the shot adds linear momentum to the swing.
A bent elbow in the drop lengthens the path and creates racket lag for greater speed.

session_ideas: Film from the side at a fixed distance with the whole body in view, 10 serves, then review the trophy position and contact height.
Shadow serves without ball, pausing at trophy to check knee bend and elbow height.
Toss-only drill: toss ten balls and let them fall, aiming for the same spot each time.
Serve from a stationary start focusing on one cue per set (leg drive, then reach up, then follow-through).

vocabulary_proposals.name: ball
vocabulary_proposals.why: Toss consistency, contact and landing cannot be judged from body features alone.

vocabulary_proposals.name: racket
vocabulary_proposals.why: Racket head position and speed define the drop and contact point more directly than the wrist.

vocabulary_proposals.name: racket_head_speed_at_contact
vocabulary_proposals.why: A direct indicator of serve power, which body-only features approximate.

vocabulary_proposals.name: toss_apex_height_and_lateral_position
vocabulary_proposals.why: Needed to judge toss consistency relative to the hitting shoulder and baseline.

vocabulary_proposals.name: angle.upper_arm_elevation_relative_to_ear_line
vocabulary_proposals.why: The tilt of the hitting arm and trunk at contact (lateral trunk tilt away from the hitting side) is not covered by angle.trunk_lean.

vocabulary_proposals.name: ball_landing_position
vocabulary_proposals.why: Required to check whether the serve landed in the service box.
